bib.title: Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only for lineage. Figure bodies are not in the text layer (only captions).

question: When does adding agents (and which coordination topology) improve or degrade LLM agent performance on agentic tasks, and can this be predicted from measurable model, task and coordination properties?
hypothesis: Effectiveness of multi-agent systems is governed by trade-offs between architectural properties and task characteristics (decomposability, tool count, single-agent baseline), not by number of agents.
contributions: Controlled evaluation of agent systems: 260 configurations across three LLM families and six benchmarks with prompts, tools and compute standardized.
Intelligence-Coordination alignment: higher capability gives linear returns but only with matching coordination structure.

Quantitative scaling principles and architecture alignment: a regression (R2_CV=0.373 Intelligence Index; 0.413 with ACI) using empirical coordination metrics; 87% accuracy selecting the best architecture on held-out configurations.

method.summary: Five architectures (single agent, and independent, centralized, decentralized, hybrid multi-agent) are run with identical tools and prompts and matched total reasoning budget on six agentic benchmarks across nine LLMs from OpenAI, Google and Anthropic (260 configurations). Coordination metrics (overhead, message density, redundancy, efficiency, trace-level error amplification) are measured from execution traces and fed with intelligence index, tool count and single-agent baseline into a 20-parameter regression of success rate, evaluated with 5-fold CV.
method.task: Agentic task success under different multi-agent coordination topologies; regression modelling of performance vs coordination metrics

inference.temperature: not stated for the main runs; temperature 0.7 used only for the K=10 reasoning traces in the information-gain estimate (App. E.5)

parameters.centralized: 3 sub-agents + 1 orchestrator, max 5 orchestration rounds, 3 iterations per agent per round
parameters.decentralized: 3 agents, 3 debate rounds, 3 iterations per round
parameters.hybrid: centralized orchestration plus limited peer communication phases (peer rounds p not numerically stated)
parameters.budget_matching: total reasoning-token budget matched, mean 4,800 tokens per trial; MAS get smaller per-agent iterations, SAS more reasoning rounds

other.stack: LiteLLM for API access, LangChain for orchestration and tool binding; API key rotation; consistent context truncation
other.agent_count_sweep: n_a in {1,3,5,7,9} for Gemini-2.0 Flash and Gemini-2.5 Pro (Fig 5)

metrics.name: Task success / accuracy
metrics.definition: Domain-dependent: factual correctness (Finance Agent), task completion (Workbench), goal satisfaction (PlanCraft), page synthesis accuracy (BrowseComp-Plus), resolution rate (SWE-bench, Terminal-Bench)

metrics.name: Coordination overhead O%
metrics.definition: (T_MAS - T_SAS)/T_SAS x 100%, where T is turn count

metrics.name: Redundancy R
metrics.definition: mean cosine similarity of agent output embeddings (also described as fraction of subtasks performed by multiple agents)

metrics.name: Coordination efficiency Ec
metrics.definition: S/(T/T_SAS), success normalized by relative turn count

metrics.name: Trace-level error amplification A_e^trace
metrics.definition: extra computational work from inter-agent coordination failures, estimated from execution-trace token analysis

metrics.name: Information gain dI
metrics.definition: 0.5 log(Var[Y|s_pre]/Var[Y|s_post]), K=10 traces at temperature 0.7, Var = p(1-p)

baselines: Single-Agent System (SAS) on same model, tools and budget
regression ablations: Intelligence + Tools + Agents; + coordination structure; + single-agent baseline; + interactions (Table 3)
capability-only model (54% architecture-selection accuracy); random choice (20%)
eval.protocol: Controlled comparison, 260 configs. Cohen's kappa for validators (Finance 0.91, Workbench 0.89, PlanCraft 0.87, BrowseComp-Plus 0.88). Naive OLS plus cluster-robust SEs (clusters = 6 datasets, CR1, t5), Holm-Bonferroni over 19 predictors, bootstrap 95% CIs (10,000 resamples) for SWE-bench/Terminal-Bench cells, leave-one-dataset-out CV, out-of-sample test on three held-out models (Intelligence Index 75).

limits: Authors concede: only 20-instance subsets for SWE-bench Verified and Terminal-Bench, bootstrap CIs about +/-20 pp per cell, pairwise comparisons underpowered.
Prompts were identical across conditions and not optimized per model or family, so architecture-specific prompt tuning may change scaling.
Only six benchmarks; no embodied, multi-user or long-horizon temporal tasks. Teams up to nine agents only on two Gemini models.

Regression clusters on dataset (G=6); several headline predictors (log_tools, efficiency x tools, baseline x agents, intelligence) are inflated under cluster-robust inference; only single_agent_baseline (p=0.004) and error x baseline (p=0.030) survive. Authors call the rest directional patterns.

Absolute cross-domain performance prediction is weak (leave-one-dataset-out); only relative architecture ranking is claimed to transfer. Out-of-sample test is BrowseComp-Plus only and mispredicts Hybrid as best.
Coordination metrics are architecture-level constants applied uniformly across benchmarks (Table 5 caption), so they do not vary within architecture across tasks.

Intelligence Index is not comparable across vendors (three models at 75 have single-agent scores 0.45, 0.36, 0.34); Intelligence Index values for several models are reconstructed/estimated by the authors, not official.
Family-specific differences are described as empirical signatures, not mechanisms.
Models used (GPT-5 era, Claude Sonnet 3.7-4.5) are dated quickly; Sonnet 3.7 deprecated Feb 2026.

terms.definition: one reasoning locus: all perception, planning and action occur within a single sequential loop controlled by one LLM instance, even with tool use, self-reflection or CoT
agents work in isolation and an aggregator combines outputs (synthesis_only: concatenation without cross-validation or voting)
an orchestrator coordinates r rounds across n sub-agents; orchestrator-to-agent edges only
all-to-all peer topology with d sequential debate rounds and consensus
orchestrator hierarchy plus limited peer-to-peer edges
each model's mean single-agent performance across all six benchmarks
measures how much extra computational work arises from inter-agent coordination failures, estimated from execution-trace token analysis
S/(T/T_SAS), success normalized by relative turn count
